203088f082d48396beb7161b.title: watchOS 27 upgrade coming to Apple Watch this month - 9to5Mac

units.text: watchOS 27 is coming this month, and now we have an official release date. Apple says we can expect the Apple Watch software update on Monday, September 14. The Apple Watch software update brings Siri AI, new ways to launch apps, and more changes to the device.
Siri AI is the biggest addition, giving Apple Watch a dedicated Siri app and a more capable assistant for answering questions. Conversations also sync across supported Apple devices.

As I wrote last week, Siri AI had a rough summer in beta, but watchOS 27 beta 8 brought a major improvement in my testing. Everyday requests finally felt responsive again, while broader knowledge questions made the watch more useful without always requiring the iPhone.
However, watchOS 27 also removes some familiar features. Walkie-Talkie is gone, and double-clicking the Digital Crown no longer provides its previous multitasking shortcut.
Pressing the Digital Crown now opens a dynamic app grid with suggested apps and Siri. The full app launcher remains available, but takes another step to reach.
Other additions include a unified Find My app, expanded Smart Stack suggestions, and improvements to Workout Buddy.
watchOS 27 supports Apple Watch Series 9 and later, Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later, and Apple Watch SE 3.
Read more in our roundup of new watchOS 27 features.
You can also learn about the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 here.
Catch up on all the Apple news around today’s event here.

units.text: IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，在 AI 照片近乎以假乱真的年代，苹果为最新发布的 iPhone 18 Pro 系列手机带来一项标注真实照片功能。

参考照片会与常规的可编辑照片并存，相当于是一个完全保持原本拍摄内容的存档图。
不过这一功能目前无法在中国市场使用。在欧盟，Apple 参考图像在 iPhone 18 Pro 机型发售时也不会提供，但运行 iOS 27、iPadOS 27 和 macOS 27 的用户可查看参考图片。

units.text: Here's What Apple Says About the iPhone Duo's Crease

Ahead of the launch of the foldable iPhone Duo, rumors suggested Apple was focused on eliminating the crease between the device's two displays. All foldables have a visible crease, and it often becomes easier to see over time from constant folding and unfolding.
On the iPhone Duo product page, one of Apple's FAQs concerns the crease. "Does the inner display of iPhone Duo show a crease where it folds?" reads the question.
Apple's response says the display is "wonderfully flat and smooth," but it doesn't say there's no crease at all and actually skirts the question it asks.

iPhone Duo features a wonderfully flat and smooth inner display with custom nano-texture finish technology to reduce glare and reflections for an uninterrupted viewing experience. The optically clear adhesives let the display layers glide as the screen folds, minimizing stress and crease.
In the press release for the device, Apple says that the Duo's nano-texture display is meant to minimize the visibility of the crease.
A premium nano-texture finish reduces glare and reflections, creating a matte surface that minimizes crease visibility and feels great to touch.

Apple does not list a fold cycle count anywhere in its press release or on its website, but it does say the hinge offers "smooth, balanced resistance for long-lasting reliability." Apple also says the hinge has more than 100 components, while the iPhone Duo has support ribs and a titanium panel under the display.
Apple competitor Samsung does list fold cycles for its foldable devices. The new Galaxy Z Fold8, which has the same general shape as the iPhone Duo, is rated for 500,000 folds.
The iPhone Duo is set to launch on October 23, with pre-orders starting on October 16.

units.text: Apple has announced that macOS 27 Golden Gate will ship to all users next Monday, September 14. Here are Apple’s official release notes for macOS 27.
Apple’s official macOS 27 release notes now available
Today alongside shipping its RC (release candidate) updates, Apple published full release notes for iOS 27 and also for macOS 27 Golden Gate.
Here are the full, unedited macOS 27 release notes:
Experience the new Siri AI

Introducing Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that’s more personal, more capable, and more conversational. It is integrated into Spotlight, so you can search for answers about almost any topic right from where you already search for things across your system. It can draw on personal context to find things across your messages, mail, photos, and more. And it can get things done across your apps, just by asking. Revisit and resume past conversations in the new dedicated Siri app, synced with iCloud across your Apple devices. Siri AI is rolling out to users, and you can get started by turning it on in Settings.
Take action on what’s onscreen

With Visual Intelligence, you can select a window of your screen and Siri can answer questions or take action with what’s onscreen, like adding events to your calendar. You can access Visual Intelligence with a dedicated keyboard shortcut — Command-Shift-Space.
Powerful new ways to edit photos

Use intelligent photo editing tools to reframe a photo after it’s been taken with Spatial Reframing or expand your shot with the Extend tool. And enhancements to Clean Up let you remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex.
New tools to browse in Safari

Automatically group your tabs into topics, so related pages are easier to find. With Notify Me, Safari can monitor pages for changes like price drops or restocks and alert you when it’s time to act. Describe an Extension lets you use natural language to create custom extensions, like adding a button to save your favorite recipes.
Easily create Shortcuts using natural language

With Describe a Shortcut, you can automate daily tasks with a simple description and all of the required steps are assembled on your behalf. For example, you can describe a shortcut to automatically text your partner when you’re headed home from work with an estimated arrival time based on traffic.
Even more refined design

Updates to Liquid Glass improve readability, and a new slider lets you customize how it looks, from ultra-clear to fully tinted. Uniform toolbars, edge-to-edge sidebars, and more detailed app icons further elevate the design.
New child safety features

Powerful new parental controls help parents more easily manage what content their children can see, who they can communicate with, and when they have access to apps. Ask to Browse requires kids to request permission before visiting any new website in Safari. Communication Safety expands its protections to help keep conversations safe. Time Allowances gives parents more flexible ways to manage the time kids spend in apps across categories, and offers guidance based on expert research that’s tailored to a child’s age. Schedules help manage which apps kids have access to at different times of the day and across the week.
A more responsive and delightful experience

An expansive set of improvements make your Mac even faster, more reliable, and easier to use. Better search in Spotlight and Mail helps you find what you’re looking for with greater ease. AirDrop Transfers and network file browsing happen faster. And many more improvements make your day-to-day use more enjoyable.
For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: support.apple.com/100100.
Some features may not be available in all regions or on all Apple devices. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/macos/feature-availability.

Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features, including but not limited to Siri AI, Intelligent Photo Editing Tools, Image Playground and AFM 3 Cloud models in Shortcuts. To learn more please visit: apple.com/apple-intelligence.
Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: support.apple.com/125039.

e5e9f162d87eb67980773eff.title: 苹果官方详解 Apple Watch Ultra 4 手表：日常续航超两天，国行 6499 元起

units.text: IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，苹果今日发布 Apple Watch Ultra 4。这块专攻运动与户外挑战的表款搭载了更先进的全新健康与健身功能，电池续航亦更持久。
Apple Watch Ultra 4 提供原色和黑色钛金属外观选项，起售价为 RMB 6,499，即日起接受订购，本月 18 日（星期五）起正式发售（点此购买）。
Apple Watch Ultra 4 搭载全新健康感测系统和 S11 芯片，带来可穿戴设备中领先的精准心率感测功能、更高频的心率与心率变异性（HRV）监测指标，更全新推出身体状态准备指数，为各界运动人士提供支持。
Apple Watch Ultra 4 还具备更持久的续航能力，在户外体能训练场景下支持最长达 45 小时的跟测，同时配备设备端 GPS 功能。
作为 Apple 迄今最强大的可穿戴设备芯片，全新的 S11 芯片不仅为健康感测系统注入动力，还将为未来新推出的功能提供支持，帮助用户随时留意重要声音，并将隐私、安全和辅助功能方面的创新置于首位。
除这些新功能外，Apple Watch Ultra 本身已通过多种方式为用户提供支持，包括覆盖各项活动的高级体能训练跟测、睡眠监测、心脏健康通知和移动心电图房颤提示软件等强大的健康功能。
心率感测技术
Apple Watch Ultra 4 经过重新架构，通过配备全新光学和电极式心率传感器的健康感测系统实现连续的高精度健康监测。
得益于这套系统和全新的 S11 芯片，Apple Watch Ultra 4 的心率感测功能精准度达到业界前沿水平。一项针对由 1000 余名受试者组成的多元化人群开展的严谨科学研究，将全新 Apple Watch 心率感测功能的准确性与领先可穿戴设备进行了比较，结果显示 Apple Watch 的准确性居于首位。
由于这枚光学心率传感器采用面积更大、能效更高的绿色 LED，Apple Watch Ultra 4 能够全天候以每 5 秒一次的频率对心率进行监测。这项持续的被动测量功能助力用户更深入了解自身的健身和生理状态，让“锻炼”和“活动”圆环更准确。通过新增的心率表盘复杂功能，用户可全天随时查看实时心率。
Apple Watch Ultra 4 经过重新架构，通过配备全新光学和电极式心率传感器的健康感测系统实现连续的高精度健康监测。心率变异性（HRV）是衡量生理压力和恢复的关键指标，其测量频率现在增加多达 24 倍，并可在心率 App 的新分区中查看。
Apple Watch 提供两种不同的心率变异性变量，帮助用户更深入地了解自己的健康状况。恢复心率变异性数据能够最有效识别日常压力与恢复信号，而整体心率变异性则能帮助用户洞察自身的整体健康状况，包括心血管健康。通常情况下，变异性数值升高表明用户整体恢复良好，下降则意味着存在压力。
依托 Apple Watch Ultra 4 更高频的心率和 HRV 跟测，新增日间生命体征视图，可供用户自行切换查看夜间和日间指标，以便在夜间指标发生变化前及早发现问题。
夜间生命体征功能现在加入恢复心率变异性指标，分析以用户的个人基线水平为参考，有助于用户更全面了解自身健康状况。
身体状态准备指数：每日体能速览
Apple Watch Ultra 4 加入全新的身体状态准备指数功能，可对用户的近期活动、训练负荷、生命体征和睡眠评分进行分析，帮助用户了解自己在未来一天中的体能状况。
准备指数每天都会在从 0 到 10 的区间内给出一个评分，并提供明确可操作的建议：“适度修整”、“量力而行”、“蓄势待发”或“火力全开”。这有助于用户决定如何度过这一天，无论他们面对的是工作日，还是要执行锻炼计划。
准备指数会随着新数据的出现全天更新，反映高强度体能训练或日间生命体征等变化。准备指数会清晰突出显示影响评分的因素，并允许用户查看更详细的信息。评分算法基于 Apple 心脏与运动研究的数据，是与 Apple 的运动科学家和医生共同开发的成果。
续航更持久
在日常使用场景下，Apple Watch Ultra 4 如今提供超过两天的电池续航时间，最长可达 50 小时。在低电量模式下，电池续航时间最长可达 84 小时。
在户外体能训练追踪场景下，当全新延长体能训练模式开启完整 GPS 和心率读数追踪体能训练时，电池续航时间最长可达 25 小时，相比前代表款延长 25%。
对于时间更长的体能训练，在最大延长体能训练模式下，Apple Watch Ultra 4 持续追踪户外跑步、步行和徒步的时长最多可达 45 小时，通常足以完成一场赛程长达 100 英里的竞赛，同时仍以每秒一次的频率进行 GPS 读取。
可穿戴设备中精准度领先的心率感测技术
计步器模型设计一新，采用新的机器学习算法和 S11 芯片，从而能够在室内步行或跑步训练期间提供更准确的距离测量结果，全天步数统计也更精准。S11 芯片还支持全新的“步数”复杂功能，方便用户直接在表盘上实时追踪步数。
依托 S11 芯片的声音识别和 Shazam 功能
由于 Apple Watch 始终佩戴在用户腕上，它是帮助用户留意重要声音的理想设备。依托内置麦克风和 S11 芯片的强劲性能，Apple Watch Ultra 4 提供多项新功能，帮助用户时刻留意周围环境。其设计以用户控制、隐私、安全和辅助功能为中心。这些功能包括：
声音识别功能首次登陆 Apple Watch，可在监听到重要声音时提示失聪或听障用户，无论用户是否随身携带 iPhone。此功能会对鸣笛、警报、门铃或婴儿哭声等声音进行监听，同时利用设备端智能技术，在检测到这些声音时通知用户。
Shazam 可即时检测用户附近播放的音乐，并自动在智能叠放中的音乐识别小组件中显示歌曲标题和歌手名，供用户在腕上轻松浏览。
苹果官方表示，这些功能不会创建或存储录音，操作系统、App、用户和 Apple 都无法访问处理时使用的原始音频。这是因为 Apple Watch Ultra 4 搭载的 S11 芯片内部采用了基于硬件的“安全隔区”设计，能在处理音频时将其与系统其他部分完全隔离，并在处理结束后立即删除音频。用户拥有控制权，并可以选择是否开启各项功能。
搭载 watchOS 27
watchOS 27 为 Apple Watch Ultra 4 带来多项额外更新，包括：
动态 App 网格会展示五个 Siri 推荐的 App 图标，这些都是用户最常用和最近使用过的 Apple Watch App。
新增单手轻点手势，用户通过食指和大拇指互点，即可方便地打开智能叠放中的小组件。现在，用户可使用轻点两下手势滚动浏览智能叠放，或者轻点一下选中某个小组件，所有操作皆可单手完成。
智能叠放小组件建议会根据场景适配显示，例如通过地图 App 推送停车位置建议，在联系人的生日临近时显示生日祝福建议。
Apple Watch 的经期跟踪功能和 iPhone 上的健康 App 提供围绝经期和绝经期提示。
表款及表带
Apple Watch Ultra 4 提供原色或黑色钛金属两种外观。今秋，各个表带系列均将增添多种全新配色。
野径回环式表带现推出深棕褐色、沙砾色、勃艮第酒红色三种配色，高山回环式表带提供沙漠色、深橄榄色、勃艮第酒红色三种配色。
海洋表带现在采用独特的半透明硅胶材料打造，并推出三种新配色：半透明灰色、半透明海藻绿色和半透明黑色。
Apple Watch Hermès Ultra 4
除原色钛金属 Apple Watch Hermès Ultra 4 外，Apple Watch Hermès 系列表带还首次推出 Grand H 钛金属表带，该款表带采用内置拉伸结构，便于调整，可服帖佩戴在潜水服外。
Apple Watch Hermès Ultra 4 还推出全新 Fathom 和 Wonder 表盘，为用户带来探索深海世界的视觉享受。旋转数码表冠，即可在展现广阔海面到深邃海底的四款表盘选项中任选其一。每个选项都将带来一种独特的蓝调和别致的动画效果。
Apple Watch Ultra 4 与环境
新款 Apple Watch Ultra 4 的设计以环保为宗旨，整体使用的再生材料占比达到 45%，包括使用 3D 打印工艺的钛金属表壳采用 100% 再生钛金属，电池采用 100% 再生钴。
Apple Watch Ultra 4 制造环节使用的全部电力均来自可再生能源，例如风能和太阳能，Apple 还已在全球范围内投资可再生能源，足以抵消用户为 Apple Watch 充电所使用的电力。与其他 Apple 产品一样，它的纸质包装采用 100% 纤维基材料，在家中即可轻松回收。

units.text: While Apple didn't talk about it during the event, press materials for the iPhone 18 Pro have revealed the release date of iOS 27.
Apple has confirmed that iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 will arrive on September 14. The updates bring a sizable collection of new features and improvements to iPhone and iPad.
Here are the updates you can expect to arrive on your devices this September.
What to expect in iOS 27

iOS 27 introduces Apple's redesigned Siri, with new models and a System Orchestrator connecting Apple Intelligence features. Siri AI adds text input, conversation history, follow-up questions, and greater access to personal context.
Visual Intelligence is now available through a dedicated Siri mode in Camera. Users can also include screenshots and captured images as context for Siri queries.
Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube

Photos adds Extend to generate content beyond an image's original boundaries and Spatial Reframe for changing perspectives. Image Playground also gains additional generation styles, including support for photorealistic images.

Parental controls simplify child account setup and expand permission requests to websites. Screen Time receives updated app controls, while Communication Safety can now detect and obscure graphic imagery.
Liquid Glass receives readability improvements, sharper icons, and additional customization controls. GymKit also lets iPhones connect directly to compatible cardio equipment.
Health seemingly didn't get much of an update this time around. Notably, Cycle Tracking adds notifications for perimenopause patterns.
Apple Maps receives updated Flyover imagery. Maps can also automatically generate Local Lists for restaurants and other locations.
The Home app can summarize notifications and describe or search HomeKit Secure Video footage. Supported HomeKit cameras can also stream and record video in 4K.
What to expect in iPadOS 27
Many changes in iPadOS 27 center on Apple Intelligence, Siri AI, and system performance. The update also includes optimizations and bug fixes.

Users running current iPadOS 26 versions should already have completed the required Spotlight reindexing. Siri AI and new Apple Intelligence features will become available across supported devices after installing iPadOS 27.
Siri AI is integrated with Spotlight, allowing searches to return results generated using Apple's AI system. The new Siri app also maintains a history of previous Siri interactions.
Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube

Siri AI can reference information from Messages, Mail, Journal, and other supported apps when responding to requests. With iPadOS 27, third-party apps can also provide information for Siri AI to reference.
iPadOS 27 also includes paste suggestions, faster windowing actions, and a new systemwide menu bar. Apple says file transfers in the Files app are up to five times faster.
The update brings changes beyond its headline Siri AI and Spotlight features. Those system improvements will be available across supported iPad models, including standard iPads and iPad Pro.

Apple is providing a live video stream on its website, on YouTube, and in the company's TV app across various platforms. We will also be updating this article with live blog coverage and issuing Twitter updates through our @MacRumorsLive account as the event unfolds. Highlights from the event and separate news stories regarding today's announcements will go out through our @MacRumors account.
As usual, Apple's online store is down for updates ahead of the event.
Sign up for our newsletter to keep up with Apple news and rumors.
Live blog transcript ahead...
8:36 am: We're on site at Apple Park, where attendees are checking in to get their badges and milling around ahead of the event. Under 90 minutes to go!
8:43 am: As usual, Apple is providing light breakfast items for everyone.
9:39 am: We're in the room!
9:49 am: The live stream is up on Apple's home page, currently displaying shifting colors and shapes in the theme of the event invite with a chill soundtrack.
9:49 am: The stream will also be on YouTube, but that typically goes live at the last moment around 10 a.m. PDT.
10:00 am: As the clock strikes 10 a.m. PDT, the music changes and the presentation begins!
10:00 am: "The following was shot on iPhone"
10:01 am: It starts with an extremely dark "movie" being shot with fire and explosions, showing some rather extreme dynamic range.

10:02 am: As Apple has been known to do recently, it is showing just how great the iPhone can look when shooting video, albeit it seems likely that all manner of high-production value add ons are being used.

10:03 am: Now we're flying over Big Sur, following a car to Apple Park... "before we reveal our main character... Not me, that's your guy." Tim Cook appears one last time, handing off to new CEO John Ternus.

10:03 am: "Our teams bring an incredible level of collaboration and care to everythign they do, all in service of a mission that has guided us from the very beginning: to make the best products in the world."

10:04 am: "The values at the heart of Apple continue to guide everything we do. As we look ahead, we see a future filled with enormous discovery and transformation. AI makes entirely new kinds of experiences possible, and AI can become even more useful when it brings together your life with the apps, services, and products you use every day."

10:04 am: "And this means the product at the center of your experiences becomes even more essential. What I like to think of as an intelligent personal hub. It's the intersection of broad new capabilities. and a deep understanding of your personal context that makes this idea so powerful."

10:05 am: "Now, if you were designing the ideal version of this hub from scratch, how would you do it? Well, first, you would want something that is always with you, deeply personal, and able to bring intelligence to the moments when it matters most. You'd require require a powerful processor that can run incredibly capable on-device models to quickly answer questions in the moment and pervasive networking to access knowledge and even more capable models in the cloud."

10:05 am: "You'd need a large, beautiful display to show rich content. You'd add high-quality cameras and microphones, so it could see and hear and reason over the sights, sounds, and the world around you. Of course, you give it all-day battery life. You'd want it to be super easy to use without a big learning curve, and finally, you'd want it to work seamlessly with your other devices, apps, and services, so it feels like one integrated experience. experience. In other words, you would arrive at something remarkably familiar, because there's no product in the world better designed to be your intelligent personal hub than iPhone."

10:06 am: "It understands your context... the most private details of your daily life. Others see that data as something to collect and store. They move it to their servers and ask you to trust them... but trust only goes so far when your data is no longer yours to control."
10:07 am: "Not even Apple can access what's yours." The Ternus era is starting with an aggressive push on privacy versus what other companies are offering.
10:07 am: "We're going to take these experiences even further with the next generation of iPhone." Starting with a shot of the moon, taken on the iPhone 17 Pro.
10:08 am: It starts with the A20 Pro, with "the longest battery life in iPhone history." "This is what happens when you go to the moon, come back and ask what's next."
It's the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. We're starting with the Pro, not the regular iPhone.
10:09 am: Comes in a deep black, a refined silver, a new "Glacier" blue, and burgandy, a "sophisticated and unique new color."
10:09 am: Apple is starting off with Apple Intelligence, pushing Apple's on-device models and Private Cloud Compute.
10:10 am: Quickly moving on to the new version of Siri. "Siri finds your personal context across apps, like Mail and Messages."
10:10 am: "Siri can take actions in your apps, including third-party apps."
10:11 am: "Have rich conversations with Siri by using voice or typing across your iPhone, or in the all-new Siri app that's right on your home screen."
10:11 am: "Siri is built right into the camera app on your iPhone, so you can ask questions and take actions, like adding multiple events to your calendar all in one go."

10:12 am: "Siri AI sounds incredible. That's because iPhone 18 Pro takes advantage of our most advanced on-device model ever, which powers expressive voices. You can pick from multiple options, then customize the pace and expressivity."
10:12 am: The new model improves on-device dictation as well.
10:14 am: "Some features will have usage limits because they rely on powerful server models. Increased access will be available with most iCloud Plus plans."
10:14 am: Now we're going deeper into the Apple Silicon in the new iPhone 18 Pro.
10:15 am: The A20 Pro is "an exceptional chip that sets a new bar for mobile computing. A brand new architecture built on 2nm technology."
10:15 am: 6-core CPU, 2 new super cores that are up to 20% faster, and 4 new efficiency cores. The super cores are "desktop class" and "the fastest in any smartphone."

10:16 am: New GPU has 7-core design with up to 40% faster graphics performance, with increased bandwidth and new neural accelerators with 2x faster 8FP math. Helps with running 3rd-party LLMs on device. The Neural Engine has been advancing year after year, with a second neural engine being added for a total of 32 cores. " A20 Pro is the ultimate chip for running advanced on-device models... this is the widest memory interface we've ever shipped in an iPhone."

10:17 am: The silicon packaging has been redesigned, with "custom packaging inspired by our M-series chips" connecting silicon and the memory directly to the vapor chamber for improved thermal performance.
10:17 am: "Effective thermal management is critical because efficient heat dissipation is what enables the maximum performance from this incredible chip."

10:18 am: "iPhone 18 Pro has a next-generation vapor chamber that helps the system manage even more heat. It has three times the surface area as the one in iPhone 17 Pro. Deionized water is constantly cycled throughout the system for significantly improved boroughs."
10:18 am: "These are giant leaps in sustained performance."

10:20 am: iPhone 18 Pro takes another massive leap enabled by A20 Pro silicon efficiencies, despite the 18 Pro's smaller size, it delivers the same battery life as iPhone 18 Pro Max. iPhone 18 Pro Max has the largest increase in battery life ever on an iPhone. 36 hours of video playback on iPhone 18 Pro, with 45 hours of video playback on the iPhone 18 Pro Max. For typical use, 18 Pro gets up to 24 hours per charge and 30 hours per charge on Pro Max. Wired charging is faster, and iPhone can charge 50% in around 15 minutes, and 5 minutes of wired charging provides 6 hours of video playback.
10:21 am: They're showing an impressive gaming demo and then quickly moving on to the camera.

10:21 am: "One of the fundamental pillars of photography is aperture. It controls how much light enters the system and affects every photo and video you take. Being able to change the aperture provides more control for light intake and depth of field."
10:21 am: "iPhone 18 Pro has a new 48 megapixel fusion main camera with variable aperture for creative control that wasn't possible before. This is the most advanced camera we've ever made."

10:22 am: "To create variable aperture, we developed a system of six laser-cut blades, each thinner than a human hair. The blades are made of a specialized polymer composite for the right balance of mass flexibility and durability."

10:22 am: "The aperture adjusts automatically based on the scene. When you're in a darker environment, the aperture opens to let in around 50% more light, like in this portrait with impressive detail and color range."
This helps explains the opening showing all the impressive dynamic range.

10:23 am: Time-lapse now supports 4K resolution in Dolby Vision HDR. "You can now get stunning cinematic mode effects from regular video after you capture, and it now supports 60 frames per second for this half-speed effect." And the new Audio Mix feature now supports music.

10:24 am: New camera feature called "Pro Controls", allowing you to change white balance or view a histogram, manually adjust the aperture and change shutter speed "for truly unique shots that weren't possible before on iPhone."

10:25 am: Pro controls work for both photos and video. "Making iPhone 18 Pro ready for everything from professional film sets to the things you should every day." Smart focus tracking uses on-device AI models to lock onto a subject and maintain detail, even if the subject leaves the screen and then comes back.
10:25 am: Improvements to photographic styles, including adjustments to skin texture.

10:26 am: "Let's talk about image authenticity..." New feature called Apple Reference Image, proving the authenticity of a photo taken on Apple 18 Pro. The main camera signs photo data at a pixel level at the time of capture. Private cloud compute turns the signed data into an unalterable image that lives in the Photos app. "It's like having a digital negative."
10:27 am: The whole event was filmed on iPhone 18 Pro.
10:28 am: "There's an upgraded dynamic island... it can now show three live activities."
10:28 am: They're giving a brief overview of what's coming in iOS 27, most of which we've seen before.
10:29 am: iPhone Handoff launches with T-Mobile and Telecom Germany. Verizon and EE launch by the end of the year, with more carriers to follow.
10:29 am: New accessories including an upgraded clear case, and new colors for the existing Apple iPhone cases and wrist straps.

10:30 am: Starts at $1199 with 256GB, Pro Max starts at $1299. There is a 2TB option now. Apple Upgrade starts at $34.99/month for 24 months (or lower with trade-in). Discounts of up to $1200 off with trade in of iPhone 14 or newer.
10:30 am: Adds AppleCare One Family option. Pre-order September 12, available September 18.
10:31 am: Interestingly, we're moving from the new iPhone Pro to AirPods — normally, headphones would come first.
10:31 am: "This is AirPods 5."

10:32 am: "AirPods 5 feature our beloved open-air fit." AirPods 5 deliver a richer, more detailed sound across a wider range of ear geometries. New active noise cancellation, with 50% more noise reduction than AirPods 4.
10:32 am: "The industry's best ANC in an open-ear design."
10:33 am: "AirPods 5 are a seamless extension of Apple Intelligence on your iPhone."
10:34 am: AirPods 5 has hands-free access to Siri with Hey Siri, as well as Live Translation.
10:34 am: "Together with iPhone, AirPods enable you to leverage the power of intelligence while staying present with those around you."
10:34 am: They're "reengineered to be more durable than ever" and more than 4 hours of listening with ANC and 20 hours total with the charging case.
10:34 am: AirPods 5 are $129, same price as the previous generation without ANC.
10:35 am: There's a second model with "some great additional features" starting with on-stem volume control.

10:35 am: "This version also has longer battery life, up to 5 hours with ANC thanks to a reengineered battery cell" and a wireless charging case with support for Apple Watch and Qi chargers. That's $149. Preorder today and available on September 18.
10:36 am: Now moving to Apple Watch.

10:37 am: "We hear from so many people about the profound impact it's had in helping them take charge of their health, stay active, keep connected to the people who matter most, and in some cases, even help save their lives."
10:37 am: New Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.
10:38 am: "This year, Series 12 and Ultra 4 take health and fitness to the next level with our all-new health sensing system."

10:38 am: "It's built on our innovative sensing foundation and improves three core elements. First, within the same small footprint, the electrode surface area is increased for better skin contact during ECG readings. Second, for better optical sensing, redesigned photodiodes are organized in a ring to capture light more efficiently. And third, larger, more power-efficient green LEDs support accurate heart rate measurements all day, even during motion."

10:39 am: It delivers higher frequency, continuous heart rate data, taking heart rate data every 5 seconds, 60x more frequently than before. Heart Rate Variability is sampled as often as every 5 minutes, 24x faster than before.

10:39 am: "We tested Apple Watch's health sensing system in a head-to-head study against other wearables using an ECG chest strap as reference, with hundreds of participants running, cycling, doing HIIT workouts. We are excited to say the results were clear: Apple Watch has the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable."

10:40 am: "Your heart rate reveals invaluable information about your fitness and current physiological state, so we're featuring high-frequency heart rate data in the updated heart rate app and new watch face complications."

10:41 am: "The health sensing system brings a completely new experience to Apple Watch readiness. Whether you're training for a race or juggling a busy week, readiness can tell you when to push and when to hold back. Each morning, Apple Watch analyzes your recent activity, vitals, and sleep to give you one score with a clear call on your body's capacity to take on the day. Recover, pace yourself, ready, go for it."
10:41 am: "This year, the Health app gets a completely new design, turning your metrics into personalized guidance with Apple Intelligence at its core."

10:42 am: "Your health over the long term is also important, so we've developed Health Age, a simple way to discover how key health metrics align with your actual age, informed by the best available science. Metrics from your Apple Watch, like VO2 Max, Sleep, and More, combined with biomarkers from your blood work to give you insight into what habits are having the biggest impact on your health age and how to improve it."

10:42 am: "And to help you build a foundation for a healthier future, there is a new longevity tab, which uses metrics from your iPhone and Apple Watch to assess your overall health across sleep, movement, hurt health, and more."

10:43 am: "You'll be able to unlock deeper insights by integrating recent lab results too. You can add them manually, sync your medical records, or in the U.S. order a full panel from Quest that features over 50 key biomarkers for $119."
10:44 am: There's a new VO2 max test where you set up your phone to watch you perform a series of exercises, getting results immediately in concert with your Apple Watch.
10:44 am: "The new Health App is coming later this year."

10:45 am: "It harnesses the power of Apple intelligence right on your wrist in a private and secure way. First, having increased awareness of the world around you is especially important for those who are deaf or hard of hearing. So, we're bringing sound recognition to Apple Watch." Can recognize sounds like alarms, doorbells, a baby crying and more.
10:46 am: Live Rewind feature "that let's you go back in time for 15 seconds." Can transcribe and show things that were just said.
10:46 am: "The next audio intelligence feature will help you remember key moments from daily conversations so you can be more present and engaged, introducing Siri recap."

10:47 am: "It uses ambient listening to take high-level notes of your conversations, like takeaways from a team meeting or a parent-teacher conference. Conversations will have an Apple Intelligence-generated title, summary, and key points. You can review them in the Siri app. You control if and when Siri recap takes notes.

When you enable it, you can choose always or set up a schedule, such as only at work or never at night. You can also turn on and off at any time, right from Control Center. Privacy is protected at every step. These audio intelligence features do not create or store audio recordings."
10:47 am: It'll be available in beta later this year, starting in English, with more languages to follow.

10:48 am: "Audio intelligence is only possible because of our new S11 chip, which is custom built to power these intelligence features while keeping your data private and secure. These features are enabled by the S11 chips power efficient always-on processor."
10:49 am: "It's not just A watch. It's YOUR watch." Series 12 comes in Space Grey, Black, Light Gold and Dark Bronze.

10:49 am: Aluminum cases now have Ceramic Shield, making screens 60% tougher. Two polished finishes in radiant gold and natural are made with titanium. Series 12 is also available in Ceramic in Pearl White and Night Blue.

10:50 am: Apple Watch Ultra 4 has a larger battery, better power efficiency, Ultra 4 gets 2 days of battery life. WIth full GPS and heart rate workout tracking, you get 18 hours, or 45 hours in max extended workout mode. Black, natural titanium. New band colors and a new titanium Hermes band.
10:51 am: Series 12 starts at $399, Ultra 4 starts at $799. Both preorderable today, available on Sept. 18.
10:51 am: Now running a new ad focused on the health benefits of the Apple Watch.
10:51 am: "The most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable."
10:52 am: "Whenever life throws a punch, Apple Watch Series 12 helps you roll with it and stay closer to every heartbeat."
10:52 am: "Your heart tells the story of your health. And it's a story worth hearing."

10:53 am: "But actually, there's one more thing."

10:53 am: "You'd still want it to fit in your pocket and the palm of your hand."
10:54 am: "Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones awkwardly stuck together."
10:54 am: "We started with the experience that we wanted for ourselves, a larger display that feels as natural and intuitive as iPad."
10:54 am: "The result is a series of remarkable innovations that we believe will redefine the experience of using a foldable phone. Here it is."
10:55 am: iPhone Duo
10:55 am: "iPhone Duo is unlike any iPhone you've experienced before. It's entirely new and at the same time remarkably familiar. The same size as your passport."
10:56 am: "The two sides connect into a continuous frame."
10:56 am: "It's immersive for both landscape and portrait use."
10:56 am: "The transition between open and closed has to be fluid and completely intuitive." The aspect ratio is the same across both displays.

10:57 am: The hinge holds the screen flat when opened. "It precisely controls opening and closing."
10:57 am: When open, it's our thinnest iPhone ever, enabled by an architecture that precisely packages key components into the camera plateau.
10:57 am: Frame is titanium, precision machined and polished to a mirror finish.
10:58 am: Essential controls are moved to the side, "placing controls within easy reach of your thumb."

10:58 am: "This meant adjusting every app's layout and reconsidering iPhone design principles that have existed for years, all to make the software and new hardware work elegantly together. The dock on the home screen is now oriented vertically. The status bar retains all the information you need in a more compact, flexible system that nestles into the corner of iPhone Duo."

10:58 am: "As you move between displays, the software gracefully expands and transitions from the outer to the inner display. Controls remain in a consistent location on the side, while content scales to take advantage of the larger screen."

10:59 am: "The system reacts as you fold iPhone Duo, reorients when you turn it on the side, and transitions to the appropriate display when you flip it over. We designed the hardware and software together to create experiences like this across the system."

11:01 am: Can also unlock iPhone Duo using Apple Watch.
11:01 am: Two colors, Star White and Night Sky.

11:02 am: "It feels exceptionally solid every time you use it." Ceramic Shield on the back, Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, and IP68 rated.

11:06 am: "Drawing on our learnings from iPad and Mac, we developed a custom nano texture finish that significantly reduces glare and reflections."

11:07 am: "iPhone Duo uses a novel structural system with a multi-layer lamination design that keeps the display flat and provides durability."
11:07 am: "Viscoelastic adhesives allow these layers to glide relative to one another during folding, like pages in a book, so the panel doesn't distort over time."

11:08 am: "A titanium plate serves as the bottom layer to bring further durability and bringing it all together is the hedge, with over 100 tiny precision components. Carbon fiber support plates create stiff, lightweight platform for the display to rest on."
11:08 am: "The result of all of these innovations is a folding display with superior viewing quality that feels premium and flat, resists wear, and meets the high standards of iPhone."
11:09 am: Up to 35% higher sustained performance than iPhone 17 Pro. Includes C2, a new cellular modem.

11:10 am: eSim only, worldwide. A separate battery on each side.
11:10 am: The two batteries operate as one battery, offering all-day battery life. Up to 31 hours of video playback on the inner display and 44 hours on the outer display.

11:11 am: iPhone Duo provides up to 24 hours of charge when using both screens equally. Fast charging, up to 50% in around 20 minutes, and up to 5 hours of video playback on the outer display after 5 minutes of charging.

11:11 am: "A key part of what puts iPhone at the center of your personal world is its incredible camera system that captures the moments that matter most. The new Fusion main camera captures incredible details."
11:12 am: Because iPhone Duo can stand on its own, it opens up entirely new creative possibilities by capturing memorable time lapses in 4K Doby Vision HDR.
11:12 am: 48MP fusion ultrawide is the same camera from iPhone 18 Pro.
11:12 am: iPhone Duo supports upgraded photographic styles.
11:13 am: 12MP Center Stage front camera on the outside screen.

11:13 am: Inner display has new FaceTime camera, works when fully open or when propped on a surface. Can dual-capture to capture front and rear camera scenes. Duo FaceTime makes video calls more fun, by letting someone with you join the conversation on the outer display.
11:13 am: Selfies improve because the outer display lets you preview the shot.
11:14 am: The screen can play animations to get your kid's attention to get them looking at the camera.
11:14 am: New Smart Take feature follows the scene and snaps the photo when the crowd is ready. No need to set a timer.
11:14 am: New accessories, including a Duo Folio with an integrated kickstand. iPhone Duo case has two separate parts that wrap around each half.
11:15 am: "The most transformational iPhone experience since the original."
11:15 am: "It's an iPhone like no other iPhone." Starts at $1999, starting at 256GB to 2TB. "We'll have great trade in offers." Preorders begin October 16, available on October 23.
11:16 am: "I hope you're as excited as I am about the all-new iPhone Duo."

11:16 am: "iPhone Duo represents the incredible creativity, ingenuity, and dedication of teams across Apple. It reflects what's possible when we bring our very best work together in service of creating something truly meaningful for our customers."
11:17 am: "These products will help people create, communicate and be more productive and entertained."

11:17 am: "They represent the very best of Apple, the curiosity to imagine what's possible, the care to get every detail right, and the conviction to build products that make a real difference in people's lives. I couldn't be more proud of the teams across Apple who made today possible. So thank you for joining us. Have a great day."

units.text: iOS 27 Available Today With These 8 New Features
Update: Apple has released iOS 27.
During its iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo event last week, Apple announced that iOS 27 will be released widely on Monday, September 14.
iOS 27 should be available around 10 a.m. Pacific Time / 1 p.m. Eastern Time today via the Settings app, under General → Software Update.
Below, we have highlighted eight new features and changes coming with iOS 27, with the main attraction being a major revamp of Siri.
iOS 27 is compatible with the iPhone 11 series and newer, but Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features are limited to the iPhone 15 Pro and newer.
New Features
Siri AI

The classic version of Siri has always been useful for basic actions like setting a timer and checking the weather, but it has notoriously struggled with more advanced requests over the years. That all changes with iOS 27, which features a much more intelligent and personalized version of Siri named Siri AI.

Siri AI is essentially a ChatGPT-like version of Siri that can answer pretty much anything. iOS 27 introduces a dedicated Siri app, or you can continue to invoke the assistant by pressing and holding the iPhone's side button. Given it is powered by Apple Intelligence, Siri AI requires an iPhone 15 Pro or newer.
Siri AI can draw on your personal information stored on your iPhone, has on-screen awareness, and can perform actions in more apps that support it.

Apple said Siri AI is limited to English to start, and the feature will be subject to daily usage limits, with expanded access to be available for a fee in the future. Siri AI will not be initially available in the EU on iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and watchOS 27, as Apple is in a regulatory battle with the European Commission.
More Apple Intelligence Features

Other new Apple Intelligence features on iOS 27 include new "Extend" and "Reframe" options in the Photos app, the ability to generate "photorealistic" images in the Image Playground app, the ability to create new shortcuts in the Shortcuts app by simply describing them, generated video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video cameras, and more.
Liquid Glass Design Changes

Apple introduced a new Liquid Glass design on iOS 26, and it has further refined the interface on iOS 27. Apple says Liquid Glass now has "more uniform refraction and improved contrast," and app icons are "sharper and more detailed."
A new slider lets you adjust how clear or tinted Liquid Glass looks.
Performance Improvements

iOS 27 makes a lot of actions and experiences faster across the operating system. For example, Apple said app launches are up to 30% faster, new photos in the Photos app library load up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers are up to 80% faster. To learn about others, check out our list of noteworthy performance improvements.
iPhone Handoff
Apple has added a new iPhone Handoff feature to iOS 27 that allows you to switch between two iPhones while using the same phone number on each device.

iPhone Handoff requires support from carriers, which may charge a fee for the feature. T-Mobile in the U.S. and Deutsche Telekom in Germany will be the first carriers to offer iPhone Handoff, with T-Mobile set to charge $5 per month for it. Apple said Verizon and the UK's EE plan to offer the feature by the end of the year, with more carriers to follow.
To learn more, read our iPhone Handoff explainer and Apple's support document. In addition, a video demonstrating the feature was shared in our forums.
Apple Cash Bill Splitting

In the U.S. only, iOS 27 allows you to split bills with a new feature powered by Apple Cash and Apple Intelligence. This capability is available in the Apple Wallet and Messages apps, or by using the new Siri mode in the Camera app.

"When users point their iPhone at a receipt using Siri mode, it can surface the relevant action to split a bill with Apple Cash and identify the items on the receipt," said Apple. "As users select their items, their total payment is calculated, including their share of tax and tip, so they can pay back exactly what they owe with Apple Cash."
Hide Location in Find My

In the Find My app, you can now share your location with others for a custom duration, such as four days and six hours. Or, you can set a set an exact date and time for your location sharing to expire. In addition, you can now pause your location sharing with specific people until the end of the day, without them knowing. The ability to hide your location is meant for things like planning a surprise birthday party for your spouse.
On iOS 26 and earlier, there are only three preset timeframes available for Find My location sharing: indefinitely, until end of day, and one hour.
CarPlay Video Apps
Back at WWDC 2025, Apple revealed that it was planning to allow CarPlay users to watch video via AirPlay in their vehicles while they are not driving.

In a WWDC 2026 video aimed at developers, Apple said the CarPlay video feature is available in new vehicles that support it. When playing a video in an iPhone app that supports AirPlay video streaming, users can select the car's display from the AirPlay menu on iOS and watch the video on a compatible vehicle's screen.
New in iOS 27, Apple is allowing developers to create CarPlay apps with video browsing capabilities, so you can find videos to watch right on CarPlay.

units.text: If you’re on the fence about installing macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple’s lengthy list of security fixes might be enough to convince you. And if you’re sticking with an older version, you may want to install macOS Tahoe 26.7 or macOS Sequoia 15.8 sooner rather than later. Here’s why.
Apple fixes 200+ macOS vulnerabilities
Apple today published the full security changelogs for macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7, and macOS Sequoia 15.8, detailing more than 200 vulnerabilities addressed in the updates.

As has been the case with several recent macOS updates, Apple’s acknowledgments include multiple AI-focused security teams and researchers, including OpenAI Codex Security, NVIDIA AI Red Team, and Anthropic Research.

Fixes included in macOS 27 address vulnerabilities that could allow malicious apps or attackers to execute arbitrary code with kernel or root privileges, escape the macOS sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper protections, modify protected system files, access sensitive user data, and more.

One AVEVideoEncoder flaw, for instance, could allow a sandboxed app to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges. Meanwhile, a UDF file system vulnerability could similarly allow an app to execute code at the kernel level. Apple also fixed vulnerabilities that could lead to remote code execution through Bluetooth, CUPS, and WebDAV.

As for macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8, the updates patch many of the same vulnerabilities, including several kernel-level, root-privilege, sandbox-escape, Gatekeeper-bypass, and remote-code-execution flaws listed above.

The older systems also feature some additional fixes not listed for macOS 27, including an ImageIO vulnerability in macOS Sequoia 15.8 that could allow arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted image.

3e4ac554b4f7f9423a98297f.discovery_title: macOS Golden Gate is here and Siri AI is its remarkable best
3e4ac554b4f7f9423a98297f.raw_lead: After months of beta testing, Apple has released macOS Golden Gate. As always, it's a mix, but there are great improvements and Siri AI is mostly fantastic.
3e4ac554b4f7f9423a98297f.title: macOS Golden Gate is here and Siri AI is its remarkable best

units.text: After months of beta testing, Apple has released macOS Golden Gate. As always, it's a mix, but there are great improvements and Siri AI is mostly fantastic.

Fantastic is a strong word but apart from a few aspects that are still startlingly poor in it, Siri AI deserves the description. Up to now, Siri has really been an iPhone tool as it was cumbersome and slow on the Mac, and simply not as useful there.
Going straight into Siri AI

Now, incorporated into Spotlight so that it is always a keystroke within reach, Siri AI transforms the macOS Siri experience entirely. Gone is the tiny popup in a corner, and what's most welcome is that the need to stop typing and wait for Siri's response is gone too.

With macOS Golden Gate, you can call up Spotlight, ask Siri AI to find that email where you told that charity some dimensions for an advert some time, and carry on working. Faster than you could ever find that three-year-old email, Siri AI is back with exactly the answer.

But truly, the fact that you can carry on working while it looks is as transformative as what it is now capable of doing. The Spotlight/Siri AI black dialog box does pop up in the middle of your screen, but you can drag it out of the way and carry on typing in your document.

I now use Siri AI whenever I want something that I know is on my Mac somewhere, whether that's a document or an email. That charity advert email was urgent but the request came when I was deep in the AppleInsider podcast, so having it just be found for me so quickly was such a boon.
I could've just searched my calendar, true. But then I asked Siri AI to find the concert tickets in one of my email accounts, and it did.

Similarly, there's a concert I was due to see last year but it was cancelled, then rescheduled, and when I suddenly worried that I'd missed the new date, it was Siri AI that said no, you're fine. You're seeing Dar Williams at this date and at this location, it told me, plus here's the email with the tickets.

On and on it goes, I'm practically at the stage of calling up Siri AI before I've finished thinking what I want. If I sound like an evangelist, it's because I now am and specifically so because macOS Golden Gate has made Siri AI so readily prominent and useful.
I would say that I no longer Google anything, I just ask Siri AI, but that's not entirely true. Siri AI doesn't always find what other AI services do, so I still keep Claude around.

Although while there presumably can't have been much work done by Apple on what it calls Siri's World Knowledge, I'm now only rarely finding Siri AI's answers to be wrong. For some reason that was different at the start of the beta test.
Siri AI always gives short answers to questions and usually they're too short.

However, for some unfathomable reason, Siri AI responses are still intentionally limited to how much you could say in a single breath. I'm sorry, but I have no particular concern over whether Siri runs out of breath or not.
So if I'm searching for something that I know will need more detail, then I will again turn to Claude.
Plus, let this be a public service announcement: Siri AI finally works with Apple Music. But only on the Mac.

Until the last moments of the macOS Golden Gate beta test, and still in the final iOS 27 beta, Siri AI would claim to be able to add Apple Music tracks to playlists. But it would then work only just often enough that you would keep trying.

Most of the time, the gigantic majority of the time, Siri AI would say it couldn't find the playlist you said. Even if just before, you had asked it to play that playlist and it had done so without complaint.

Apple Music and Siri AI integration was, and still is on iOS, enraging, partly because of how patronizing it could be. If you keep asking, Siri AI will eventually apologize for your confusion, as if it's you who is getting this wrong.
It was not chance that means Siri AI has been coded to say "I won't respond to that" when you tell it just precisely what you think of it.

I should be ecstatic that it's now working on the Mac, but on the one hand, I almost always use that particular feature on the iPhone while driving. And on the other, there was a whole twenty minutes during one beta release where it worked on the iPhone too.
You can't believe the surprise when Siri AI finally added an Apple Music track to a playlist, like it always said it could.
There weren't that many people using the beta, compared to how many will now have it. But Apple has the problem of convincing those beta users to try this feature again.
Which feels like an own goal because Apple already had the much greater issue of getting anyone to try Siri at all. Apple broke Siri two years ago and then left it like that.
Deep breath.
Nonetheless, you must try Siri AI on macOS Golden Gate and by itself, it is the reason to upgrade. You have to get on a waitlist, though.
What else macOS Golden Gate brings

Saying that Siri AI is the reason to upgrade is of course a way of stressing just how good it is, when it's good. But this is also close to strictly accurate as the only major update to macOS this time is Siri AI.

So there are refinements to Liquid Glass, for instance, but they're really just a sop to the vocal minority who don't like that redesign. Apple can tell you that there are now controls for adjusting just how liquid its Liquid Glass features are, for instance, and it's not lying.
There is a slider to adjust how liquid Apple's Liquid Glass design is, but it doesn't make much difference.
But you have to whack the slider fully to one way or the other to really distinguish any difference at all. Since I'm fine with Liquid Glass, I tried this, shrugged at it, and never went back.

Your mileage may vary, as alongside this overall Liquid Glass slider, there are improvements to individual elements. So you could fill your time trying out variations on the appearance of Dock icons, and that might be worth it.

I say that particularly because while I haven't done any of that appearance fiddling, Apple has. This is just me, I realise, but somehow through the betas I kept mistaking the Preview icon for the Keynote one.
L-R: The Keynote icon, the original Preview icon, and the final Preview one.

They're not even really that close, but something about them kept tripping me up. Then in the latest betas and now in the final release, Apple has changed the Preview icon and I no longer choose the wrong one.
Mind you, I prefer the previous Preview icon.

One other change during the beta process was that Apple removed the old toggle for turning off Apple Intelligence. I wondered at first whether that meant everyone was stuck with Apple Intelligence, but there is now a Turn Off Siri control which may do the same thing.
There's no toggle for turning off Apple Intelligence any more, but there is one for turning off the whole of Siri. Though you won't want to.

I wouldn't know, really, because originally I wasn't bothered by Apple Intelligence in any sense of the term. And now, specifically because of Siri AI, and specifically because of how it is on the Mac, Apple Intelligence is part of my daily workflow and I've no interest in turning it off.
Shortcuts

While Shortcuts works across the iPhone and iPad as well, I am most often creating them on the Mac. Which means my second favorite aspect of macOS Golden Gate is how Apple Intelligence has changed Shortcuts and made it much quicker to use.

Unfortunately, for several years, the Shortcuts action to open a Safari tab group has failed on the Mac. It works fine on the iPhone and the iPad where it's of little use, since you're already tapping on the screen.
The new Shortcuts app is very good at clearly saying what a Shortcut it creates will do. Except it sometimes doesn't do anything of the sort.
On the Mac, it would be so convenient to press a keystroke or tap a Stream Deck button to switch between Tab Groups. And you were supposed to be able to do exactly that.
You still can't, and some time in the last few beta test versions, Apple implemented a kind of solution. It removed the Open Tab Group action from the Mac.
It's unfathomable why Apple couldn't make this work when it added the action. But it's more unfathomable why the new Shortcuts will pretend to do it.
Seriously. It's a bad part of what is otherwise a brilliant feature, which is the Apple Intelligence version of Shortcuts.
Previously, Shortcuts would offer countless actions that you could drag into a list which it would then work through. You can still do this and you can still create complex Shortcuts by hand.
You can tell Shortcuts what you want in plain English and while far from flawless, it is remarkably good at creating just what you need.

But Apple has added Apple Intelligence to the simple plus button that gets you started. Once you click that, Shortcuts just asks you what you want to do, then it does the job of choosing the actions and assembling the Shortcut to do it.

There are times when this is so good that it is amazing and you think you'll never fashion a Shortcut manually again. For instance, there's a timing thing I need for the AppleInsider podcast and I could never quite work out the math, but Shortcuts did it immediately.

Yet there are times, such as with the Safari tab groups example, where Shortcuts will tell you that it has done what you asked. It will present a concise list of what precisely that Shortcut will do for you, even if it will not do anything of the sort.
It's not surprising that there are limits, of course. But it is surprising that there are these failures when sometimes Shortcuts will display an error message saying it can't do a particular thing.
So Apple Intelligence in Shortcuts is like Apple Intelligence in Siri AI. Absolutely fantastic, except when it's pants.
Shortcuts can build reasonably complex Shortcuts automatically.
Nonetheless, the ability to incredibly quickly make at least basic Shortcuts by just saying what you want, that's transformative. More Mac users will get into Shortcuts because of this.

And while I actually enjoy writing Shortcuts for myself, most of the time now I do start by asking for what I want. Of the last 20 Shortcuts I've made, all of them started this way, although 5 failed.
That's still a 75% success rate, which could well be better than my own.
Surprisingly useful Photo tools
Just as on iOS 27, macOS Golden Gate also includes Image Playground and it has been improved. I've not used it once for serious work, but I do see the improvement.

That's because for some reason, and who knows why, I once asked the previous version to create an image of five clowns carrying a horse. That version gave me too few clowns, too many horses, and looked dreadful.
That image is actually far better than the first betas of Image Playground could produce. But I asked for five clowns, not seven.
Trying the same prompt now, the image is vastly better and there is only one horse. But for some reason there are seven clowns. They seem happy.
What I have used for actual work is the way that Photos can now edit images. I was making a poster for my YouTube channel and needed more space for the text, so I had Photos extend my image.
It took moments. Open Photos, pop the image in, choose Edit, Tools, Extend, and then drag across where you want to widen the image. It didn't take Photos much longer to do the job.
And let this be proof of how well it did it. I did this a couple of months ago and staring at my YouTube channel, I cannot now remember or even guess which poster I did this with.

That was a real use-case for me, but I did experiment with the other photo manipulation features early on in the beta and originally had more limited results. So limited that I did not again try reframing a shot to move someone's eyeline, and I did not try to erase large sections of the image ever again.
Don't look at my silly hat, look at the Apple Store to the right. There was a whole person there before. And my own right arm is AI-generated.
Until just now. Trying it out again now, the results are staggeringly better than they were.

It must depend on the shot, but I had one of me and my wife in Vancouver, sitting against a glass partition in that city's great Apple Store. For obvious privacy reasons, I just now used Clean Up to remove my wife and I tell you, if we ever divorce, I'm going to use this instead of cutting up all our printed photos.

Clean Up removed her, and filled in the space not with some generic background, but what looks to me like what really was originally behind her. It has taken a sliver of an Apple Watch poster and recreated that, plus put some of those Apple Store wooden cube seats there.
But then I reframed it because for some reason I wasn't quite looking at the camera. It's like I thought I was a YouTube presenter or something.

There was only a slight reframing adjustment needed, but it did it. It did it with finer controls than there were and, most importantly for me, it did it so well that it truly looks like I was staring into the camera.
But to do that, I noticed that it filled in some more of the background around the edge of the frame. So I tried telling it to extend more and I chose the most difficult part.
In this shot, I am leaning into frame from the left, so I extended it out in that direction. And Photos made up my arm and jacket perfectly.
I'm still going to tell people to look into the lens, please. But what seemed like a toy at the start of the beta test is now a usable, potentially useful feature.
Writing Tools are a shrug, but a useful one
This bothers me because it's creating some material and I never imagined I'd do that. I'm certainly not going to be using macOS Golden Gate's Siri AI to write anything.

Although... It's now 31 years since Microsoft Word added red underlining for spell-checking and that means for three decades I've barely paid any attention to it. That's an exaggeration, but it's definitely true of the blue underlines you get when Word is bored and decides to make up grammar rules.

Yet during the beta test of macOS Golden Gate, I've been more conscious of Writing Tools. Never the actual feature, I don't think I've opened those more than once, but the gentle automatic underlining as I type has been rather good.
Once, Siri AI also went ahead and corrected the spelling in my document too.
Plus there was a time when, as I'm in England, I wasn't certain of the US spelling of a word. I called up Spotlight, asked Siri AI, and it told me I'd got it wrong, which was helpful.
Every time, too, I can type "Fix it" into Siri AI and it does, it amends my text. Once it just did that anyway: told me it was wrong, corrected it in my document and said "you're welcome."

Okay, it didn't say that, but it was still startling to see it happen. I don't understand why it did this that once, but even being able to ask it to fix the spelling of one specific word seems good to me.
Fantastic, staggering, and dreadful

You can tell I like macOS Golden Gate and you won't be remotely surprised to learn that I do not want to go back to macOS Tahoe. But it isn't all brilliant, and there are annoyances even beyond the peculiar problems with Shortcuts.

I say annoyances. Some are minor and actually I'm certain they are only because I'm writing this while still on one of the last betas. There's a bug right now about when you scrub through a video; the slider keeps snapping back to the start, for instance, and that will surely be fixed.
Or there is that great feature when you're saving a document and can click on the name of an existing one. That copies the existing name and you can just make some changes.

So I'll have video assets such as "Take 1" and can just replace that digit with 2 rather than typing out the whole name. That's been a thing on the Mac for as long as I can remember, but in the last betas it was working too quickly.

I would be in the Save dialog, move to a new folder, and find that my document title was immediately changed to that of something already there. It always seems to happen when I've taken the time to write a new document title, too, and that gets wiped out.

Similarly, a bug I've had that appears to still be here is that menus in Save dialogs won't always work. In Pixelmator Pro, for instance, I can't always specify that I want to export an image as PNG instead of JPEG because the menu flips back closed too quickly.
Of course the Phone app has separate audio controls from System Settings, although at least they are now under "Audio" instead of "Video."
But if there were one Mac thing I would wish Apple would fix... no, okay, one thing other than Shortcut tab group support, it is the Phone app.
This should be extraordinarily useful. To be able to make and receive calls on the Mac without getting out your iPhone, it should be so very handy.
But it does not work.

There has been one minor improvement. Originally it was that despite any other sound setting on your Mac, the Phone app had its own. It would sometimes even default to something you no longer had connected.
True, once you knew it did this ridiculous thing, you could change the audio setting. Once you also knew that to change anything to do with audio, though, you had to look under the Video menu.

This is now better. That same menu has been retitled Audio. Although while that lets me specify what microphone and speaker I want on one Mac, on another it won't. It just snaps back to whatever it was set to by default.
But it doesn't help even when you can set these. I have the correct microphone and speaker selected in it, but if I call someone, they cannot hear me.
I'd obviously like that to be fixed, please, and I struggle to understand why the problem hasn't been resolved yet. But then maybe I'm just a heavier phone user than most.

Only, since I am, I would also like to be able to answer or end calls with a keystroke or a Stream Deck button. As it is, I have to wait for the call notification to appear, then find the green answer button.
Even Keyboard Maestro clicks on that Answer Phone icon to no avail.

That notification is now appearing quicker than it did, so it's no longer the case that people have hung up before it's displayed. But clicking on that green answer button is a lottery because sometimes it just does not respond.
You could blame my hand/eye coordination, except for this. I went to the trouble of making a Keyboard Maestro macro and including in it a screenshot of that button.
Now I press a Stream Deck button, it launches that macro, Keyboard Maestro looks for the button, finds it, clicks it, and nothing happens.
I'd phone Apple to ask them about it, but...
Devils and details
The more you dig into anything, the more likely you are to find problems. I'm conscious that in the case of macOS Golden Gate, what are truly small irritations still manage to burrow under my skin.
I think you can rightly criticize me for that, it is surely a sign that I need to get out more. But perhaps it's also a sign of how important macOS is to me.

If you are a Mac user, it has always been astounding how much you can do with these devices. I've a relative who believes I am a computer geek because I'll spend 15 hours in front of my Mac, but to me that's not what I'm doing at all.

I'm writing articles, I'm editing video, I'm reading books, I am doing countless things that I need and enjoy and relish. A new macOS is just about the only thing that touches every part of that, every application, and every task.
So a new macOS is an enormous deal. And while I initially thought that Siri AI was the sole update in macOS Golden Gate, I do now see that there is more.
It's still the main update and it's still fantastic. But overall macOS Golden Gate is yet another example of how Apple makes you wonder why you put up with the previous version at all.

units.text: iOS 27 Now Available: 10 Features to Try First

Today is the official launch date of iOS 27, which means it's available for everyone that has an iPhone 11 or newer. ‌iOS 27‌ introduces Siri AI, tons of new Apple Intelligence features, Liquid Glass updates, and performance improvements to make your iPhone feel faster.
Performance Improvements
Apple sped up a long list of features in ‌iOS 27‌, and it's immediately noticeable when you download the software.

Everything feels faster than it did in iOS 26. Animations are quicker, apps launch faster, and AirDrop transfers complete faster. You'll see improvements when taking photos, opening the keyboard, using the App Library, and swapping Home Screen pages. Your iMessages between devices sync more accurately, messages won't fail to send and will be automatically retried, and your iPhone can transition more smoothly between Wi-Fi and cellular.

The majority of new features in ‌iOS 27‌ require ‌Apple Intelligence‌ and an iPhone 15 Pro or later, but the under-the-hood improvements are available on all iPhones, so even older iPhones will feel faster. For more on what's new, we have a list of the best performance improvements in iOS 27.
Siri AI

‌Siri‌ AI is the new version of ‌Siri‌. It's more like ChatGPT or Claude ‌Siri‌ in ‌iOS 26‌, with support for back-and-forth conversations. ‌Siri‌ AI can do a lot of what other AI chatbots can do, but unlike other AI options, ‌Siri‌ has private access to your messages, emails, photos, apps, and other personal data so it can complete a wider range of tasks. ‌Siri‌ can also search the web, so it can answer all kinds of queries.
You can activate ‌Siri‌ with a wake word, swipe down from the middle of your screen to type a question to ‌Siri‌, chat with ‌Siri‌ in the ‌Siri‌ app, or press the side button to activate ‌Siri‌.
Some examples of what ‌Siri‌ is now able to do:
Create home automations with a command like lock all the doors at midnight.
Find specific emails, messages, photos, images, links, files, and other documents people have sent to you. You can ask based on person, time, location, and more.
Delete files, emails, photos, or messages.
Add all items from a recipe on a website to a shopping list.
Recommend activities, places, and restaurants you might like based on what it knows about you.
Look at something on your screen like a website and answer questions about it.
Answer general knowledge questions.
Add information about people to the Contacts app when asked, like birthdays or additional phone numbers.
Find passwords for websites and apps that are stored in the Passwords app.
For more on some of the commands you can use with ‌Siri‌, we have a dedicated Siri AI guide.
Visual Intelligence
Visual Intelligence is now in the Camera app, and you can get to it by swiping to a new ‌Siri‌ mode that's available as an alternative to the photo and video modes.

There are new ‌Visual Intelligence‌ features, and ‌Siri‌ can do things like tell you the nutritional value of something you're about to eat, or calculate what everyone owes from an image of a receipt. We have more examples in our iOS 27 Visual Intelligence guide.
Write with Siri

‌Siri‌ can generate text from scratch in ‌iOS 27‌, and there's a system-wide Write with ‌Siri‌ feature you can get to from the keyboard. ‌Siri‌ can help you write, give you feedback on what you've written, change the tone or wording of your writing, and even write in your style by analyzing your emails and messages.
Your iPhone also automatically suggests grammar fixes in addition to spelling fixes.
Photos Clean Up

The Clean Up tool that removes unwanted objects from images in the Photos app is much improved in ‌iOS 27‌, and it does a better job cleanly removing what you don't want and filling in what's missing more convincingly.
There are also new Extend and Reframe image tools for extending the borders of a photo using AI and changing the perspective or composition of an image.
Our full iOS 27 Photos guide goes through all of the new features.
Adjust Liquid Glass

There's a new Liquid Glass slider that lets you choose how clear or opaque you want your buttons, toolbars, and menus to be. Get to the new slider in the Settings app by choosing Appearance and then tapping on Liquid Glass.
Safari

You can create custom extensions with natural language commands in Safari, which is useful for when you want to do something specific but there isn't a good extension available. Some sample suggestions, from Apple:
Create a citation for the current webpage and copy it to my clipboard
Create a 3-minute focus timer for the page
Set the minimum font size to 14pt
Turn the page into pirate speak
Style websites like 90s websites with bold colors and type
Every time I open a new tab, draw me a different flower
Highlight and show the dimensions of webpage elements when I tap on them
Enter the design mode for a website so that I can edit the contents
Safari can also automatically organize your tabs into categories and watch a webpage and let you know if there are changes. For more, read our iOS 27 Safari guide.
Home App

Use HomeKit Secure Video cameras? They now support 2K and 4K recording. There's also a new AI feature that gives you text descriptions for what's happening in your home, and there's an option to search through videos using natural language to find something you're looking for.
The AI features require a 2TB iCloud+ plan for one camera and a higher plan for more cameras, but the 4K streaming doesn't.
For more on what's new in the Home app, check out our iOS 27 Home guide.
AirPods EQ

If you've ever wanted to adjust the sound of your AirPods, you can do so with new AirPods customization options that let you tweak mids, highs, and lows. Custom EQ is available for AirPods 4, AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2.
Shortcuts

If you find the Shortcuts app intimidating, it's easier to use in ‌iOS 27‌. You can tell the Shortcuts app what you want to be able to accomplish with a shortcut, and it'll make it using AI. You can then refine it with further natural language requests, or manually edit.
More on Shortcuts is available in our Shortcuts guide.
How to Install iOS 27
You can install ‌iOS 27‌ the same way any iOS update is installed. Open the Settings app, go to General, tap on Software Update, and wait for the ‌iOS 27‌ update to pop up.
Apple will also send out prompts suggesting that users upgrade to the new operating system.
More iOS 27 Info
If you want to see a complete list of the features available in ‌iOS 27‌, you can find that information in our full iOS 27 roundup.

Between the official release of its 2027 operating system updates, point updates to previous operating systems, and standalone updates to Safari and Xcode, Apple today rolled out security fixes across dozens of devices.

When it comes to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, Apple’s security content page lists more than 120 fixes, some of which address vulnerabilities that could allow attackers or malicious apps to execute arbitrary code, gain kernel or root privileges, access sensitive user data, bypass system protections, and more.
